Error message index¶

This index lists every error and warning message that users have quoted in the forums and pages used for this manual, together with the context in which it appeared, its cause, and the fix. The messages are copied as users posted them. Numbers inside a message (file names, array sizes, process IDs) change from run to run; they are shown either as in the original report or as <N>.

Entries are sorted alphabetically by message text. The sort ignores case, the rank prefix 0: that Priroda puts in front of messages from process 0, and leading punctuation such as ***. Each entry says how well its fix is supported:

  • confirmed means that the user who had the problem, or several users, reported that the fix worked;

  • single report means that one user, usually an experienced one, posted the fix and nobody confirmed it.

Messages from MPI, Cygwin and the shell, which Priroda does not print itself, have their own section. Messages for which no fix is known are collected under Unresolved. For problems that print no message at all (silent hangs, ignored settings, wrong results), see Solving common problems.

Note

Most of these reports come from Priroda 6 to 17 (2009–2018). Messages and behaviour in current builds may differ, and none of the entries has yet been reproduced with a current binary.

Messages printed by Priroda¶

application called MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1) - process 0¶

The run stops with this line from the MPI library. Two causes are known; a third case is under Unresolved.

  1. Hybrid functional with theory=dft.

    • Context: 2014 builds. The output shows Basis set input: './basis.in' twice and then stops; the summary box (| Number of atoms) never appears. Happens with B3LYP or PBE1 under theory=dft.

    • Cause: hybrid functionals are supported only with theory=ridft. Older versions ran such input without a message and silently dropped the exact exchange.

    • Fix: use theory=ridft. See Hybrid functional silently ignored.

    • Support: confirmed by several users (the same sample input ran with ridft and failed with dft).

  2. Relative paths in a parallel run.

    • Context: Linux, 2012, run started through the bundled mpiexec. The output stopped after the list of nodes while all cores stayed at 100%.

    • Cause: the basis file was given by a relative path.

    • Fix: start the binary itself with -np N and give absolute paths for the binary, the input, the output and the basis file inside the input.

    • Support: single report (the user who had the problem).

Basis set input: 'basis4.bas'   1?¶

  • Context: Windows, 2013, relativistic basis file basis4.bas / basis4.in. The job stops at this line.

  • Cause: the scalar-relativistic Hamiltonian was not switched on.

  • Fix: add four=1 to $control.

  • Support: confirmed by the user who had the problem.

Cannot open input file '<path>'.¶

  • Context: Linux, 2012; the user’s command line was ./p6_64.bin /home/quantum/pridoda/task.in /home/quantum/priroda/task.out.

  • Cause: the input file did not exist at that path (here the directory name was misspelled, and the parent directory did not exist either).

  • Fix: check the path with ls -l; work in a directory you own, cd into it and run ./p task.in task.out. See The input is not read, or is read wrongly.

  • Support: resolved in the thread.

For the Windows message cannot open input file, see Unresolved.

dipole =   0.000000 au (  0.000000 D)¶

  • Context: version 6, relativistic basis sets; the dipole was zero for every molecule, even with task=dipole.

  • Cause: a limitation of version 6.

  • Fix: upgrade; version 8 and later print a value.

  • Support: two users.

*** error in '$scf' : unknown name erations¶

  • Context: 2015 builds, $scf containing both iterations= and convergence= (for example $scf restrict=0 procedure=BFGS iterations=999,999 convergence=1e-10 $end).

  • Cause: a parser problem with this pair of keywords. One user found that the group was read only when iterations came before convergence; another got this error in either order. A third report says the pair works only together with procedure=bfgs.

  • Fix: put iterations before convergence, on separate lines, and check the scf options: line in the output to see whether both values were read. See convergence.

  • Support: the reports conflict; not confirmed.

error opening file ''3z.bas''¶

  • Context: IRC input, 2010.

  • Cause: the basis file name was enclosed in two single quotes.

  • Fix: use one pair of straight double quotes, basis="3z.bas", or an unquoted absolute path. Typographic quotes copied from a document fail too.

  • Support: single report for this message; the quoting rule is repeated by several users.

For all methods the performance will be degraded terribly if more than one process read and write large files on the same physical drive!¶

  • Context: quoted in a 2014 forum post as a warning, by a user running 16 processes with all scratch on one disk. The same sentence, with “except GGA DFT” after “For all methods”, is a note in the input.txt keyword list, so the post may have quoted the documentation rather than program output.

  • Cause: all processes write their scratch files to the same physical drive.

  • Fix: give each process its own drive with a colon-separated path list, or keep scratch in RAM with a negative disk value. If neither is possible, the run still works, only slower. See Memory, disk and scratch errors.

  • Support: the documentation gives the same advice.

h = -25.15!¶

  • Context: SCF table of a diverging DFT run (2014, energy about −2800 hartree). Preceded by hmin = ... values that grow in magnitude.

  • Cause: the SCF is running away.

  • Fix: cap the SCF at iterations=10, save the vectors with $control save=, restart with $guess read=1, and repeat. See SCF does not converge or diverges.

  • Support: the restart technique is recommended by experienced users on both forums; the asker did not report the outcome.

lowest eigenvalue = <N>!!!¶

  • Context: Priroda 6 on Windows, 2015. Large negative values (-1814.64!!!, -788121.66!!!) from the first iteration on; the energy rose every macro-iteration and the run ended with no convergence! and SCF is far from convergence.

  • Cause: not established. Likely contributors in the reported case: a non-native basis with diffuse functions, the hybrid B3LYP with theory=DFT, mult=0 for an odd number of electrons, and a poor starting geometry.

  • Fix: correct the input first (multiplicity, theory=ridft for hybrids, a native basis, a sensible geometry), then try procedure=bfgs with more iterations and a finer grid. See SCF does not converge or diverges.

  • Support: suggestions from two experienced users; the asker did not report back.

0: malloc(<N>) failed¶

  • Context: seen as malloc(536870912) failed, malloc(1678770176) failed. and, on a cluster, 0: malloc(<N>) failed. The number is the request in bytes.

  • Cause: Priroda could not allocate what memory (plus a RAM disk from a negative disk) asked for. The 32-bit Windows (Cygwin) builds cannot allocate more than about 1 GB.

  • Fix: ask for less than the machine has free. With a RAM disk, memory + |disk| (MB), times the number of processes, must fit in physical RAM; for example memory=9000 disk=-14000 on a 24 GB node. On 32-bit Windows, use at most about 1000 MB (512 MB was enough for most DFT jobs), or use a 64-bit build. See Memory, disk and scratch errors.

  • Support: confirmed by several users.

malloc: using debugging hooks¶

  • Context: Linux, 2012, first line on the terminal. In one case it was followed by [0] MPI Abort by user Aborting program ! and [0] Aborting program!.

  • Cause: on its own the line is harmless; one run that printed it was simply still running, and its output file appeared later. The abort lines appeared when the input file could not be found.

  • Fix: if the abort lines follow, check the paths of the input and output files (see The input is not read, or is read wrongly).

  • Support: single thread.

molecule input: ''¶

Priroda prints this line before it reads the molecule. When the run stops right after it, the next lines tell the cause.

  1. Followed by a mangled keyword and ?, for example ' ?matrix, ?rtesian or 'z-matrix' ?.

    • Cause: the input has Windows (CRLF) line endings, or was saved as Unicode or from Word.

    • Fix: convert to plain text with Unix line endings (dos2unix input.in). Avoid Cyrillic letters and spaces in host, directory and file names.

    • Support: confirmed by several users.

  2. Followed by illegal charge/multiplicity.

    • Cause: atomic numbers written as real numbers (25.0) in $molecule.

    • Fix: write atomic numbers as integers.

    • Support: single report.

  3. Followed by 'cartesian and ' ?, together with OOPS: semop lock failed 98304.

    • Context: Linux, 2012, normal user; the same input worked on Windows and as root.

    • Cause: probably CRLF line endings (the line break after cartesian points to a stray carriage return).

    • Fix: dos2unix; chmod +r on the input files was also suggested.

    • Support: not confirmed; the thread does not say whether it was fixed.

no convergence!¶

  • Context: printed when the SCF reaches its iteration limit without converging. It is usually followed by SCF is far from convergence.

  • Fix: see SCF is far from convergence.

OOPS: semop lock failed¶

  • Context: shared-memory runs. Reported (a) in v6 on 7 cores during a DFT optimization, together with process N received signal 2 or 6; (b) after another fatal error, for example 0: out of disk space (VNNNN), 18067356KB; (c) on Linux for a normal user but not for root (OOPS: semop lock failed 98304).

  • Cause: a failure of the semaphores used between processes. In case (b) it is only a consequence of the first error.

  • Fix: (a) use fewer cores (in v6, at most 4 for an optimization and 2 for a Hessian); cleaning up semaphores with ipcrm did not help. (b) fix the first error. (c) unresolved.

  • Support: (a) and (b) each from one thread. See Parallel and MPI problems.

0: opening file /tmp/tmpNNNN.0¶

  • Context: Windows builds (2009). The output ends here, just after the System options block shows Disk:   1 GB '/tmp'.

  • Cause: no scratch directory was set, and Windows has no /tmp.

  • Fix: add $system path=. $end (or path=/cygdrive/c/temp), or set the TMPDIR environment variable. See path.

  • Support: confirmed by several users.

0: out of disk space (VNNNN), <N>KB¶

  • Context: conventional MP2 runs (2010), and a correlated Hessian on 16 processes (2014). Variants seen: 0: out of disk space (VNNNN), 184441541KB, 0: out of disk space (VNNNN), 542865328 and 0: out of disk space (ci.Rnvvo), 553912160.

  • Cause: the job needs more scratch than disk allows. The limit is per process.

  • Fix: raise disk=; for MP2, use theory=rimp2 instead of conventional MP2; check that cartesian or z-matrix matches the coordinates actually given. See Memory, disk and scratch errors.

  • Support: confirmed; the 2014 Hessian ran after disk was raised to 40 GB.

0: output file 'tasK.out'?¶

  • Context: Linux, 2012, printed when the output file name contained capital letters.

  • Cause: not known.

  • Fix: use lower-case file names.

  • Support: single observation, not explained.

process 0 got signal 6¶

  • Context: geometry optimization, 2026. On the last step the INTERNAL COORDINATES table ends with too few.

  • Cause: the optimizer could not build a valid set of internal coordinates.

  • Fix: $optimize cartesian=1 $end (see cartesian).

  • Support: single report (answer by an experienced user; the asker did not report back).

0: read file ./tmp/tmpNNNN.0 (VNNNN): fd=3 buf=<address> siz=8 lpos=0¶

  • Context: conventional MP2, 2010.

  • Cause: given the same diagnosis as out of disk space: not enough scratch.

  • Fix: as for out of disk space.

  • Support: single report.

SCF is far from convergence¶

  • Context: the SCF has used up its iterations and the gradient is still large; Priroda stops. Reported with diverging DFT runs, non-native or diffuse basis sets, and transition-metal complexes.

  • Cause: see the possible causes in SCF does not converge or diverges.

  • Fix: check the input (multiplicity, theory=ridft for hybrids, native basis, reasonable geometry). Then restart from the saved vectors (iterations=10, $control save=, $guess read=1, repeat), or switch the SCF procedure: $scf convergence=1e-7 procedure=bfgs iterations=250 $end with $grid accuracy=1e-9 $end.

  • Support: the restart technique is recommended by several experienced users and automated in the limor1 pri script; neither fix was confirmed by the users who asked.

Solving for responses ...¶

  • Context: not an error: the run hangs at this step. Version 6, analytic Hessian on 4 cores.

  • Cause: limited parallel support in version 6.

  • Fix: use at most 2 cores for a v6 Hessian; better, use version 16 or later.

  • Support: single source; another user ran DFT Hessians on 24–32 cores without trouble.

Vicinity of a Stationary Point(?) --- STOP.¶

  • Context: first point of an IRC (2014), followed by IRC> point   1: distance = ... and a REACTION PATH with a single point.

  • Cause: the energy did not decrease on that step.

  • Fix: change the IRC step (radius): larger for a very flat barrier top, smaller for a narrow barrier such as a proton transfer.

  • Support: single report (experienced user).

0: write VMNN(<N>:<N>)?¶

  • Context: seen as 0: write VMNN(11753704:14042536)?. A 7-atom RI-MP2 energy with four=1, basis4.in and set=L22 (2015). The same job also reported that it did not fit in memory, whatever memory was given.

  • Cause: apparently a bug in the stored-integral RI-MP2 path for some basis and size combinations.

  • Fix: $integral direct=1 $end (see direct).

  • Support: two users reproduced the problem and the workaround.

Messages from MPI, Cygwin and the shell¶

chown: cannot access '/home/username/.gvfs': Permission denied¶

  • Context: printed by chown -R run as root on a home directory while fixing file permissions (Linux, 2012).

  • Cause: a GVFS mount point that even root cannot enter.

  • Fix: none needed; it is harmless and unrelated to Priroda.

Error in system call mpiexec: No such file or directory¶

  • Context: Linux, 2012, Priroda started as mpiexec -np 4 p file.in file.out. Also seen: mpiexec could not exec p.

  • Cause: the binary was not found through the bundled mpiexec.

  • Fix: start the Priroda binary itself, which takes -np: ./p -np 4 file.in file.out, with absolute paths if needed.

  • Support: confirmed by the user who had the problem.

If 'p6_64' is not a typo you can use command-not-found ...¶

  • Context: Linux shell, 2012.

  • Cause: the current directory is not in PATH.

  • Fix: run the binary as ./p6_64 ... or by its full path.

Sorry!  You were supposed to get help about: agent-not-found¶

  • Context: Windows, Cygwin OpenMPI 3.1.3, 2018, command orterun.exe -np 2 p6.exe test.in test.out. The output continues with [[INVALID],INVALID] FORCE-TERMINATE AT Not found:-13 and a segmentation fault.

  • Cause: the user was running version 6, which has no parallel support of this kind.

  • Fix: use version 16 or later (version 17 was recommended).

  • Support: single report; the asker did not report back.

tcp_peer_send_blocking: send() to socket 12 failed: Transport endpoint is not connected (128)¶

  • Context: Windows, Cygwin OpenMPI parallel run (2018) on a PC connected by WiFi that also had a LAN adapter.

  • Fix: disable the unused LAN adapter.

  • Support: single report.

Warning: '/dev/shm' does not exists or is not a directory.¶

  • Context: Windows 10 with Cygwin (2016); printed when Priroda was started from cmd.exe but not from the Cygwin shell.

  • Cause: outside the Cygwin shell, the Cygwin libraries do not find their environment.

  • Fix: start from the Cygwin shell, or create dev\shm and dev\mqueue one directory above the one Priroda starts from. See Parallel and MPI problems.

  • Support: recipe from two experienced users.

Unresolved¶

No fix is known for the following messages. Where a reply suggested a direction, it is given, but nobody reported that it worked.

application called MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1) - process 0 during task=anharmonic¶

  • Context: 2011, task=anharmonic with four=1 and basis4.in. The run died after the first displacement, at the line Scalar Relativistic Density Functional Calculation:.

  • Notes: no reply. The four=1 combination may be involved; this is a guess.

cannot open input file¶

  • Context: Windows, 2011, p6.exe input.in output.out with the executable, cygwin1.dll, the inputs and the basis folder in one directory.

  • Notes: changing to that directory first did not help. Other users pointed to a launcher script that sets TMPDIR and changes to the program directory, and to input encoding (Word, Unicode, CRLF). The thread never found the cause.

MMDYNAMIC  need 'mmdata'¶

  • Context: version 9, the undocumented MMDYNAMIC task.

  • Notes: the task needs a molecular-mechanics data file that is not distributed.

process 0 received signal 1¶

  • Context: DFT on a Pt complex with an rL33 relativistic basis (2010); the SCF table showed hmin = -0.302.

  • Notes: one user suggested checking that the basis table has no zero entries, that is, that every element is present in the chosen set. Another user’s H2 RI-MP2 test with the L33 basis worked.

process 0 recieved signal 11¶

  • Context: Windows, 2013, first optimization step of Hg and Os porphyrins with 3z.bas; the Ru analogue worked. (The spelling recieved is as posted.)

  • Notes: 3z.bas has no relativistic corrections but should in principle work. For Hg and Os the recommended route is basis4.in with four=1; the crash itself was not explained.

We need 1.5 GB of memory...¶

  • Context: 2020, ordinary PC, $system ... disk=40. The message is quoted only up to this point.

  • Notes: one reply suggested that it refers to RAM (memory=), so more disk space would not help. Not confirmed.

0: write file /tmp/tmpNNNN.NN (leAX): fd=<N> buf=<address> siz=<N>,<N> lpos=<N>¶

  • Context: 2020, cluster, analytic Hessian of a 142-atom chain (OLYP/4z.bas, memory=9000 disk=40), after several iterations of ANALYTIC SECOND DERIVATIVES OF SCF ENERGY. Seen as 0: write file /tmp/tmp9633.11 (leAX): fd=21 buf=0x2aaaae307e80 siz=9525120,3885400 lpos=996398760.

  • Notes: no direct answer. Replies in the same discussion pointed out that path= was not set, so scratch went to /tmp, which on a cluster may be small or quota-limited, and suggested a proper scratch directory or a RAM disk. A full disk or a file-size limit is a plausible cause, but this is a guess.
